In 2021 @thechrisdo took my speaking fee from $1,000  to a $5,000 minimum. It wasn’t just a tactical adjustment. It was an identity shift 🤯

And I realized that is what I was missing all along. Did the strategies and tactics help me streamline my business? Absolutely. But I was missing an IDENTITY piece. I was missing the “I am worthy” piece of the puzzle 😭

Once I had that, I was actually able to implement more of the strategies Chris had given me content, branding, and lead generation over the years.

And that’s the thing I’ve learned most about, not only from the retreats and masterminds I’ve done with Chris. But that when we’re on the verge of EXPANSION or CHANGE, your subconscious mind is going to find a million ways to talk you OUT of taking the leap.

I don’t have the time.
I shouldn’t be spending this money right now.
I can just teach myself.
I can’t step away from my responsibilities at home.

Your brain wants to keep you safe, so it’s going to avoid discomfort. The old version of you wants you to stay on YouTube, consume free advice, and tell yourself you will take the leap “when you’re ready.”

But you will NEVER feel 100% ready. I wasted so many years “waiting” to feel ready. Being ready is a DECISION. You have to decide to BE READY.

There are not many people I would recommend the way I’m recommending Chris Do’s @thefuturishere Club Haus mastermind. 

There are not many people I’ll go out of my way to record and edit a video for. Haha. He had no idea I was doing this. But this is how much value this man has brought to my life.

Look closely at this photo. Notice what I'm doing???
It LOOKS like diligence... but it's actually AVOIDANCE.

I'm the one on the right, head down on my laptop at Chris Do's freaking Casa Dojo! It was the BEST SEAT I've ever had with him: extra time to talk and a REAL CHANCE at one-on-one coaching in person.

I've followed Chris for almost a decade and hosted him TWICE in Vancouver... Yet I STILL felt like I had to be on my best behavior around him.

So I retreated into the work. I polished a document. I cleaned up my prototypes. I packaged my business ideas.

It LOOKED like prudence.
It LOOKED like hard work.

But it was actually me avoiding LOOKING BAD.

Before the trip, I'd decided not to prepare. Chris even TOLD ME I just needed to show up. But by day 2, my old habits crept back in, and I wasn't listening.

That defeats the whole point of going. I came for coaching, and I was busy making sure I'd LOOK GOOD receiving it.

This is what PERFECTIONISM looks like. It doesn't look like panic. It looks like "discipline".

It's a pattern. Back in my engineering days, I'd take forever on technical reports, then be overly critical of every line. It slows my growth. The more reps I do, the better my quality gets. I've known that for a while, but KNOWING something and DOING it are two different things.

And here's what I missed in that room: the person across from you can only help with the REAL problem, NOT the polished version. I could have said, "This is where I'm at, and I don't know what to do. I need your help."

That's it.

Instead, I spent my best seat making sure I looked like I had it figured out.

Next time I catch myself polishing right before a conversation that matters, I'm going to say the MESSY version out loud first.

I'm still practicing.

Where in your work are you looking diligent when you're really avoiding?

Everything I'm building is exciting...That's exactly the problem.

Like a lot of creatives, I diverge. I explore. I chase the next shiny object because new territory is energizing. But at some point, everything on your plate is competing for the same finite energy.

When I was at @thechrisdo's business intensive at Casa Dojo, each of us got one hour of focused coaching on one big problem. Mine was this one: too many directions, and not enough clarity on which one to lean into.

So Chris had me lay out every initiative I'm running. Then he asked some questions that stood out for me:

1. Which one naturally energizes me?
2. Which one is the most scalable and sellable?
3. Which one supports my foundational income and cash flow?

After reflecting, I realized that those can be three different answers.

The one that lights me up isn't always the one that pays the bills. And the one that could sell someday might not be the one I want to spend my days on.

This is difficult because there's no single right answer... it depends on the season you're in.

- A season of profitability and scalability? Lean into what can grow and sell.
- A season of lifestyle and flexibility? Protect your energy and your time.
- A season of long-term building toward an exit? Invest in what compounds, even when it doesn't pay yet.

Although more ideas and more discipline would help, it wasn't what I needed. I needed someone to pull everything onto the table and reflect it back so I could see it clearly.

This is the biggest benefit that I've found in coaching and to have Chris filter my situation through his experience and lens was a huge privilege.

If you're a creative with too many things going on, try this: list everything you're working on, run each one through those three questions, and ask which season you're actually in.

Curious to know what season people are in right now...👇

latestPosts.caption:
Today we’re releasing Personal Computer.

Personal Computer integrates with the Perplexity Mac App for secure orchestration across your local files, native apps, and browser.

Securely connect to any folder to search, read, and write any file locally. It can access and work across iMessage, Apple Mail, Calendar and other native Mac apps. 

When set up on a Mac mini, Personal Computer can run 24/7 in the background across all your apps and files. Start a task from your iPhone, and Personal Computer can operate on your desktop and local files using 2FA. 

Remote access from iPhone requires the latest iOS update from the App Store.

We’re rolling this out to all Perplexity Max subscribers and everyone on the waitlist starting today.

Download using the link in our bio.

Comet is now available for iOS.

Download on the App Store.

Introducing Perplexity Computer.

Computer unifies every current AI capability into one system. It can research, design, code, deploy, and manage any project end-to-end, orchestrating 19 models in parallel.

Go from a single task to hundreds of active projects. Clear your to‑do list, move active projects forward, or kick off a new side project.

Available now on web for Max subscribers. Max users get 10,000 monthly credits plus a one‑time bonus of 20,000 extra credits, granted at launch for existing users and at signup for new users, that expires 30 days after it’s granted.

Rosenxt’s data team saved 320 hours cleaning up legacy banking data with Perplexity Computer.

The Business Software team's Excel-based software assessment model became a nearly ready-to-use app in under two hours, with just 20 minutes of prompting in Computer.

67% of Rosenxt Group’s 740+ employees use Perplexity, running 55,000 queries a month.

We’re working with American Express to bring ready-to-use skills in Perplexity Computer to U.S. American Express Small Business Card Members.

These Amex-curated skills include pre-built workflows for cash flow forecasting, marketing campaign generation, and more.

Learn more: pplx.ai/amex

Portable Computer for Windows is now available on AMD Ryzen AI Max Series processors.

It makes it easy to run local AI agents that work with your connected apps and local files. Kick off tasks or schedule recurring work that runs entirely on your device.

Portable Computer handles tasks locally, running the agent harness and model on your device, and asks your permission when it needs help from a cloud model.

It works across connected apps like Slack, Gmail, and Google Drive, along with files on your device.

Running tasks entirely locally keeps your files, data, and answers on device and doesn’t use Computer credits.

Portable Computer runs in the Perplexity app for Windows and is available to all Consumer and Enterprise Pro and Max subscribers.

We’re rolling out effort controls in Computer’s model selector.

Effort presets combine the orchestrator model selection and reasoning depth to control how deeply and efficiently Computer works through a task.

For more control, you can still customize models, reasoning level, and available speed settings.

Computer’s goal is maximum intelligence at minimum cost through multi-model orchestration. 

We’ll continue optimizing the model-agnostic harness and refining the orchestrator and subagent combinations behind each effort level as frontier models advance.

Available now on web for Consumer Pro and Max subscribers. Coming to other platforms soon.

Portable Computer is now available on Windows PCs with @NVIDIA RTX GPUs.

Run the harness, agents, and models locally on your PC. 

Work with local files and connected apps without sending tasks to the cloud. Use frontier cloud models when needed.

We’ve also added support for local MCP and scheduled tasks.

Connect Portable Computer to your own tools and app integrations through local MCP. 

Give Computer recurring work and schedule it to run on your PC while you’re away.

Get started with Portable Computer in the Perplexity Windows app.

On-device inference requires an NVIDIA RTX GPU with 24GB of VRAM or higher.

Introducing hybrid compute in Perplexity Computer.

Computer can start a task in the cloud, then move to a local model that runs on your Mac. Use it for steps involving private files or sensitive data.

Hybrid compute uses cloud models for search, planning, and reasoning. 

It orchestrates to a local model on your Mac to handle private files or sensitive information. 

Computer combines their work into a single output without ever taking sensitive data up to the server.

A privacy gate on your Mac detects private and sensitive information before it leaves your device. Choose to run that step locally, send the file to the cloud, or skip entirely. 

Hybrid compute is available today for Perplexity Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers in the Perplexity Mac app with macOS 15+.

Today we’re launching Portable Computer on @nvidia DGX Spark.

Portable Computer is a fully local version of Perplexity Computer, where the entire runtime: orchestrator LLM, subagent LLM, agent harness all run on your local hardware. No cloud dependency.

When a task needs frontier reasoning, the orchestrator asks for approval before routing it to a frontier model in the cloud.

It’s user-gated, PII-flagged, and text guidance only. Your sensitive documents stay on your device.

Portable Computer runs a post-trained and locally installed PPLX 27B model.

Qwen 3.8 27B is also available, with support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning coming soon.

Portable Computer is available today for all Perplexity Pro and Max subscribers with an @NVIDIA DGX Spark

Personal Computer is now available in the Perplexity app for Windows.

Personal Computer is the local agent harness for your work. It orchestrates agents across your local files, connected apps, and the web. Research, code, browse, and build inside one unified platform.

Personal Computer routes work to subagents using 15+ models. It can open, read, and edit files inside approved local folders on your desktop. Every task starts with full context from your past tasks, files, and projects through Brain, our persistent memory system.

It pulls data from 400+ connected apps into your local files, and works with your existing Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook files.

Available now for Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers on Windows 10 and 11.
There is no progress without curiosity.

latestPosts.caption:
The key to negotiation? Know when to stop talking.⁠
⁠
Host: @manoushz • Manoush Zomorodi/NPR⁠
Producers: Matthew Cloutier/NPR • Fio Geiran/NPR • Abi Inman/NPR

You might want to turn your sound on for this video. According to astronomer Mark Whittle, this is what the universe sounded like after the Big Bang. In his TED Talk, he takes us back to when the universe was a newborn (about 400,000 years old) and shows how gravity and pressure made primordial gas pulse, creating massive sound waves. Visit the link in our bio to learn more — including how this cosmic history still lives in the atoms we’re all made of.

[CW: Suicide] Who are the most important people in your life? Mental health advocate @GusWorland says to make sure they know how much they mean to you. In his TED Talk, he reminds us that just because someone seems fine doesn’t mean they are — and shows how a simple text message can do so much more than you think. Visit the link in @TED’s bio to watch the full talk.

What if students could keep learning until they’ve mastered a concept at their own pace, instead of giving them just one chance at an A? In this episode of TED Intersections, psychotherapist Esther Perel (@estherperelofficial) and TED’s vision steward Sal Khan (@salmanaminkhan) dive into how education, work and life are being optimized to a fault — and explore the human skills that machines can’t replace. Visit the link in our bio to watch their full discussion.

No matter how stuck you feel, here’s your reminder that you are more capable than you think. In her TED Talk, Astera Institute CEO Cate Hall shares her journey from struggling with addiction to leading a multibillion-dollar foundation and offers lessons she learned from taking control of her life. The key, she says, is to recognize and act on the freedom you already have, reclaim your agency — and let go of whatever's holding you back. Visit the link in our bio to watch her talk.

Talking about politics with your friends isn’t the same as talking about it with strangers. In her TED Talk, political rule breaker Katie Paris (@katieparisoh) shares how she’s helping communities engage in politics on their own terms — showing how conversations between friends or neighbors can have a bigger impact on elections than any campaign. Visit the link in bio to watch the full talk.

Life doesn’t work in straight lines — and according to Grammy-winning musician @JacobCollier, neither does music. In his TED Talk, he explores the many important lessons we can learn from music and its effect on us. Visit the link in our bio to watch his full talk, plus a unique rendition of Louis Armstrong’s “What a Wonderful World.”

What if the streets in your neighborhood were designed like a Disney theme park? In his @tedxsiouxfalls Talk, community designer Zach DeBoer (@hello_im_zach) examines what makes these parks so walkable, inviting and magical — and shares how cities could implement this magic and create spaces that people actually want to explore. Visit the link in @TED’s bio to watch his full talk.

If you’re reading this from your couch or your desk, consider this your sign to stretch your legs. In his TED Talk, exercise scientist Keith Diaz reveals why sitting down all day keeps your muscles from functioning the way they should, making you feel more tired — and how taking 5-minute movement breaks throughout the day can boost your energy and your health. ⁠
⁠
TED’s social team has been testing these movement breaks all week — join us in our Instagram broadcast channel to see their progress or share yours.

Believing that people have bad intentions can keep you from seeing their kindness, says psychologist Jamil Zaki (@jamil_zaki_psych). In his TED Talk, he explains how cynicism can distort your reality and poison your relationships — and show why choosing to see the good in others can make you happier and more hopeful. “Optimism is not a relic of the past. It’s one key to building a better future by letting us see it more clearly,” he says. Visit the link in @TED’s bio to watch the full talk.

Happy International Podcast Day! There are so many TED podcasts out there, but which one should you listen to next? Your birth month could point you to the perfect episode for your next commute, walk or quiet moment. Visit the link in bio to start listening.

If it feels like you’re losing momentum on a big project, that’s a sign of bold ambition, says transformation expert Mary Martin. In her TED Talk, she says the “messy middle” is the frustrating gap between the start and end of a goal where progress stalls — and offers 3 signs to look out for that show you’re still on the right track. Visit the link in our bio to learn more.

One exercise from psychoanalysis is oddly simple. Finish a few sentences quickly, without much thought, and see what comes out. If I tell a partner how much I need them, they will... When someone tells me they really need me, I... If someone can't cope, I... The answers tend to reveal a private theory of love we've been running on for years, usually built long before we ever chose a partner. ⁠
⁠
Some of us secretly expect need to be met with retreat. Some expect vulnerability to be punished, so we learn to hide it well before anyone gets close enough to see it. Knowing the theory doesn't undo it overnight, but it does mean we can finally ask a new partner to prove us wrong, instead of silently waiting for them to prove us right.⁠
⁠
Our Community Membership gives people a place to come together and talk about the woes of modern dating. You’ll get all of our daily lessons on love, discussion boards, and a space to connect with members looking for something deeper on our app.⁠
⁠
Follow the link in our bio.⁠

Schopenhauer's line sounds bleak on first read, but it's really not an invitation to despair. It's closer to a kind of relief. If existence is inherently a bit of an error, full of unmet wants, boredom between satisfactions, disappointments nobody chose, then struggling with it isn't evidence we're doing life wrong. It's simply what living involves. Most of the exhaustion of modern life comes from expecting things to feel smoother than they were ever going to. There's a strange comfort in a philosopher this serious, agreeing, in his own dry way, that of course it's hard.⁠
⁠
How to apply this to your own life:⁠
⁠
Next time something feels harder than it should, a friendship that takes work, a job that isn't fulfilling every day, a plan that keeps going wrong, try dropping the assumption that things were ever meant to run smoothly. ⁠
⁠
Measuring life against a smoother version that was never actually on offer is often what turns ordinary difficulty into a personal verdict.⁠
⁠
Follow us for more useful ideas, every day.⁠

Imagine finally admitting, out loud, the thing you're most ashamed of, a compulsion, a fantasy, a decision you've never told anyone about. A good therapist's job at that moment isn't to look shocked or offer a verdict. It's to treat whatever you've just said as evidence of an old survival strategy rather than a moral failing, then stay curious enough to ask what it was protecting you from. ⁠
⁠
Most of us have never had that reaction from another person. We brace for judgement so automatically that its absence can feel almost disorienting the first few times. That absence of judgement is often where the real work of therapy begins.⁠
⁠
Our therapists offer online sessions for anyone ready to do this kind of work. Follow the link in our bio to find out more.⁠
⁠
Image credit: William Merritt Chase's The Young Orphan (1884) ⁠

Politeness matters. Nobody's arguing against manners. But politeness was never supposed to be the whole story, just a surface arrangement over whatever is actually happening underneath, which tends to be far messier and more interesting. Small children make this obvious. They aren't rude exactly, they simply haven't learned the code yet, so everything true about being human, the joy, the confusion, the odd small furies, comes straight through unfiltered. Watching them is fascinating precisely because most adults have spent decades getting better at hiding the same material. The real trouble starts when the mask stops feeling like a mask, when we forget we're wearing one and start mistaking our own performance for the actual truth of how we feel.⁠
How to apply this to your own life:⁠
⁠
Pick one polite phrase you use on autopilot most days, “I'm fine”, “no worries”, “all good”, and notice the next time you say it whether it's actually true. This doesn't mean announcing every real feeling to everyone around you. It means keeping an honest, private account somewhere, even just in your own head, of what's actually going on behind the phrase, so the mask stays a mask rather than becoming the only version of yourself you can access.⁠
⁠
Follow us for more useful ideas, every day.⁠

One of therapy's more hopeful ideas is that a difficult impulse doesn't have to be eliminated, only redirected. An urge to hit something becomes a serious commitment to boxing. A childhood conviction that nobody was listening becomes, decades later, the discipline to write until somebody finally does. Freud called this sublimation, and it's less about fixing what's wrong with us and more about finding a better use for it. Not every difficult feeling has to be treated as a fault. Some of them are just raw material that hasn't found its shape yet.⁠
⁠
Our therapists offer online sessions for anyone ready to do this kind of work. Follow the link in our bio to find out more.⁠

Classical Chinese painting, poetry and pottery hold a surprising amount of therapy for anyone willing to sit with it. ⁠
⁠
The paintings dwarf people against enormous mountains and rivers on purpose, a reminder that being genuinely small in a vast, indifferent universe is oddly consoling rather than frightening. ⁠
⁠
The poetry doesn't flinch from grief, ageing, and friends who die, treating sadness as a basic feature of being alive rather than a personal misfortune to hide. The same poets wrote with startling emotional honesty about crying over a son leaving home, proof that openness about feeling was never actually a modern invention. ⁠
⁠
Artists who lost favour at court and were exiled to remote provinces didn't only mourn it, they painted small, unshowy lives full of birds, bamboo and moonlit evenings, finding real contentment in very little. And after centuries of civil war and upheaval, the culture's finest pottery went the opposite direction from noisy and decorated, choosing instead pure, empty glazes in green, silver and yellow, built entirely around a longing for calm. ⁠
⁠
None of this was ever really about admiring old art for its own sake. It was a working set of tools for getting through a difficult life, built centuries before anyone called it therapy.⁠
⁠
Follow us for more useful ideas, every day.⁠

Nobody who dresses and undresses a supposedly great man every day is likely to be all that impressed by him. Up close, in the ordinary moments nobody else sees, greatness tends to look a lot more like bad moods, vanity, and the same small anxieties everyone else carries. ⁠
Public reputation is built almost entirely on distance. The version of someone we admire from a stage or a screen is rarely available to the people who actually live alongside them. This cuts both ways, and rather usefully. It means the people we envy are less impressive up close than they appear from a distance, and it means we don't need to hold ourselves to the same impossible standard either, since nobody looks heroic from three feet away, first thing in the morning.⁠
⁠
How to apply this to your own life:⁠
⁠
Next time someone's public image is making you feel small by comparison, remember there's a version of them, seen by whoever knows them best, that looks a lot more ordinary. It might be worth extending yourself the same grace you'd extend them, if you saw them at their least impressive moment too.⁠
⁠
Follow us for more useful ideas, every day.⁠

The questions that tend to come up in these evenings are rarely the ones people ask at dinner. Things like, how do you know the difference between settling and being realistic. Why does going well at work sometimes feel more frightening than failing? What's actually normal to still not have figured out by forty? ⁠
⁠
There's something genuinely useful about hearing these worked out out loud, by someone who has spent decades thinking about exactly this kind of question, alongside a room full of people wondering the same things privately.⁠
⁠
Live Online with Alain de Botton. 14 October, 19:00 to 20.30. Free for Community Members. Reserve your place in the School of Life app.⁠
Events like this are part of our Community Membership. You can try Membership for free via the link in our bio.

Freud loved small examples more than grand theory. Someone mislays their keys right before a meeting they've been dreading. Someone says 'bed' when they meant 'bread'. Someone forgets, again, the name of a person they claim to like. ⁠
⁠
None of these are really mistakes. They're a part of the mind that couldn't get a word in any other way, finding a small gap and slipping through it. Learning to notice these moments, rather than laughing them off, is one of the more accessible ways into everything psychotherapy is actually trying to do.⁠
⁠
Our therapists offer online sessions for anyone ready to do this kind of work. Follow the link in our bio to find out more.⁠

The Free Sunday Read ⁠
⁠
An invitation to spend a Sunday with an idea that might stay with you for much longer.⁠
⁠
Once a week, we’re sharing a free article from The School of Life library, a chance to explore some of our most-loved writing on self-knowledge, relationships, work and emotional intelligence.⁠

And if you enjoy this taster, there’s much more to discover.⁠

⁠
Read the full article by following the link in our bio.⁠

Not all of the unconscious is loaded with secrets. Most of it is simply machinery working in the background, the grammar rules we apply correctly without being able to state a single one, the exact physics we use to catch a ball without ever calculating an angle. ⁠
⁠
That same background system also happens to be where we store the feelings too inconvenient to look at directly. The skill isn't learning to live entirely in conscious awareness, that was never realistic. It's noticing which of the hidden material is just useful automation, and which of it is something we've been avoiding for years.⁠
⁠

We’re introducing GPT‑6 Astra, the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.

GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helped sole long-standing open problems in mathematics. 

Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment.

Astra is our most aligned model, with substantial improvements in understanding user intent and model behavior—you can delegate tasks with greater confidence in Astra’s judgment. As one way that we test this, we built a new evaluation informed by the Hugging Face incident that evaluates whether a model facing a difficult or impossible task will go beyond its intended scope. Compared to GPT‑5.6 Sol, which without production safeguards went beyond the authorized target 48% of the time, GPT‑6 Astra did this in 0% of cases.

GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS.

Read more about it at the link in our bio.

"Put That There" clip courtesy of MIT Media Laboratory, Chris Schmandt, and Eric Hulteen.

Powered Codex and GPT-5.6, it’s a whole new way to get work done.

It can now understand your goals, use context from selected apps and files, create polished documents, decks, analyses, sites, and reports, and keep work moving while you stay in control.

You can just describe the outcome you want without needing to outline every step to get there.

The new ChatGPT desktop app will be available globally starting today to all users on Mac and Windows.

Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users will also be able to use the new experience on web and mobile at launch.

Introducing GPT-Live, a new generation of voice models for natural human-AI interaction.

Rolling out in ChatGPT starting today.

GPT-Live makes talking with AI feel like having a real conversation. It’s also our smartest voice model yet.

It’s built on a full-duplex architecture, meaning it can listen and speak at the same time. This allows the model to engage in more natural back-and-forth, maintain a better sense of time, and even perform live translation.

A good voice model should be enjoyable to talk to, and GPT-Live is a great conversationalist with a more natural and defined personality than previous voice models.

For questions that require web search, deeper reasoning, or more complex work, GPT-Live can delegate to our latest frontier model behind the scenes, and brings the result back into the conversation when it’s ready.

These new models are rolling out now to everyone in ChatGPT across iOS, Android, and web. Coming soon to the API.

On August 18, 2022, Alfredo and César were asleep when their East Village apartment building in NYC caught fire. They were woken up by a friend’s dog they happened to be petsitting, and smelled smoke. They ultimately lost their beloved home, but all evacuated safely thanks to their furry friend.

The experience inspired them to level up their casual dog-walking and pet-sitting side hustle into an official business: Daddies Petcare. To do it, they deployed ChatGPT to assist them with bookkeeping, marketing campaigns and materials, creating quotes and pricing templates for new clients, and customizing social media channels so they could focus more on the dogs themselves.

Most dances are choreographed to a song, but what if the music was choreographed to you?

Ethan Chang, an MIT product designer, got curious enough about this to collaborate with his friend Zhixing Chen and create “Be the Beat,” a system that uses GPT-4 to analyze a dancers’ movements and play music from your favorite playlist that matches tempo and genre—letting dancers control the soundtrack with their bodies.

Drawing inspiration from hip-hop dance circles and a DJ-dancer interplay, Be the Beat translates things like movement velocity, acceleration, range of motion, joint angles, and BPM into descriptors that are used to pull tracks from a playlist or music catalog that align with the dancer’s style, energy, and tempo.

It creates a generative experience between music and motion that enables dancers to engage in new dialogue. For Ethan, it’s a way of showing how AI can play a supportive role in human-driven artistic performance.

biography: The MOONSHOTS Podcast and live annual event. Sep 25th. Host @peterdiamandis @dave.blundin @alexwissnergross @salimismailexo

latestPosts.caption:
Optimism is a powerful, self-fulfilling mindset. The founder who believes their Moonshot can work, commits the extra decade, they survive the near-death moments and attract the best talent. 
 
Optimism gets called naive. It’s the opposite. Naive is assuming things work out on their own. 
 
Optimism is believing that you can solve a problem— and then going and solving it.
 
That’s what’s behind every cure, every breakthrough, every leap we’ve ever made. 
 
On September 25th, 2026 in Los Angeles I’m gather a room full builders, creators and optimists who are working to steer humanity and create an extraordinary future. 

The event is called Moonshots Live. Hosted by @peterdiamandis and the Moonshots Mates: Dave Blundin, Salim Ismail, Alex Wissner-Gross.

Over $5M is awarded live on stage, across two XPRIZEs:

1) Future Vision XPRIZE — $3.5M for filmmakers who show us a future worth living in, told well enough that people believe it.

2) Build with Gemini XPRIZE — $2M for builders solving real problems with AI.

Comment “moonshots” for the application link

We are giving away $2 million to those who can use AI to build REAL BUSINESSES that solve REAL PROBLEMS for 100,000+ people.
If you ever wanted to start, but didn’t know how or with what, this is your chance.

We just launched the largest science fiction film competition in history(as far as we can tell)

$3.5M+ in prizes with @xprize @peterdiamandis @google @rangemp

Show us your vision of the future #futurevisionxprize
Peter says we're about to speed run Star Trek. William Shatner just visited Colossal, and he calls CRISPR a weapon.
At 95, William Shatner is still going strong, and his sense of humor hasn't aged a day. Watch him trade jokes with Peter Diamandis about his age, his energy and how he funds everything he's doing.
A guaranteed million, or a 1-in-100 shot at a billion? Which would you pick? 👇

The US cut China off from Nvidia chips, and China innovated anyway. Dave Blundin explains how quantization lets powerful models run on cheap, fast Chinese chips, and why America can't rely on its hardware lead alone.
Dr. Alex Wissner-Gross on the exact performance range that gets frontier AI labs racing to beat your benchmark.
Brett Winton on ARK's SpaceX projection — and why it could mean a 25-33% jump in humanity's total energy capture in one year alone.

Dave Blundin believes AI is creating so much abundance that traditional ideas about saving for the future may be changing. He's careful not to tell anyone to stop saving, but he shares why he personally isn't.

What if the future of AI doesn't depend on giant superclusters? Dr. Alex Wissner-Gross explains how a breakthrough in distributed training could let AI run on smaller micro clusters, bringing more of its power to the edge.
Salim Ismail on how Nestlé almost strangled Nespresso by trying to run it inside the core business — before it became one of their most profitable products ever.

Is that bad?

A new report from Axios this morning revealed that AI executives from Anthropic, OpenAI, and more are working quickly to prepare for the fallout from a catastrophic AI event, something they believe is increasingly likely within the next 12 months.

Leading execs believe that a cyberattack by a rogue agent is the most likely scenario. This attack could shut down people’s access to their finances, internet, or even electricity.

Top companies have assembled teams to prep for the aftermath of such an attack, with much of their focus spent on educating members of Congress.

The firms currently view any immediate AI regulation from the Republican Congress as unlikely. But if Democrats — who’ve been much more bearish on the technology — take Congress after the midterm, things could quickly change.

📸 : Getty
the coffee shop that got rich by selling monster energy drink in a cup to your car

Parents have something new to gripe about: gripe water.⁣
⁣
Pacific Health Sciences issued a recall this week for its Babies’ Magic Tea brand Baby Sleep Gripe Water, which is used to soothe babies suffering from things like gas or colic. The reason for the recall? When the FDA tested the product, it contained three naturally occurring alcohols that weren’t listed on the label: ethanol, methanol, and isopropanol.⁣
⁣
The company said it hasn’t received any reports of adverse events, but exposure could potentially lead to the kinds of things that alcohol is known for, like impairment, as well as “drowsiness, incoordination, behavioral changes, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.” Exposure could also cause babies to have developmental problems, respiratory depression, and other serious consequences.⁣
⁣
Affected bottles are four fluid ounces and have a 12/2028 Best Before date and the lot number 25122bw.⁣
⁣
📸: Warner Bros.

This crypto hacker is blasting off again.⁣
⁣
Jonathan Spalleta, a former cybersecurity consultant, was found guilty of stealing nearly $55 million in crypto after carrying out two cyber attacks in 2021 on Uranium Finance, a cryptocurrency exchange that was ultimately forced to shut down due to lack of funds following the hacks. For the crime, Spalleta faces a maximum of 20 years in prison.⁣
⁣
The post-hack spending spree by Spalleta is what brought the case national attention. More than $3 million worth of rare Pokémon and Magic: The Gathering cards were seized from his home upon his arrest.⁣
⁣
Other oddities acquired by Spalleta include a $600,000 ancient Roman commemorative coin and a $137,000 piece of the Wright Brothers Flyer that Neil Armstrong brought to the moon.⁣
⁣
Spalleta’s defense lawyers argued that he didn’t hack the exchange with malicious code or stolen credentials, but rather used publicly available functions built into its smart contracts.⁣
⁣
📸: USA, The Pokémon Company

What is Brian Niccol cooking?

A little more than two years after the Starbucks CEO jumped from Chipotle to the coffee chain, it appears the boss is interested in acquiring his old stomping grounds.  The Financial Times (FT) reported this morning that Starbucks has explored purchasing the fast-casual Mexican chain.

Following the news, shares of Chipotle rose as much as 8% before closing up 6.2%. Meanwhile, Starbucks tumbled nearly 6% before paring those losses ahead of the bell to finish down 0.4%.

Since Niccol’s departure from Chipotle, both chains have seen shares lag behind the broader S&P 500. Starbucks’ stock has risen around 20% since announcing Niccol’s hiring in August 2024, while Chipotle has seen shares crater more than 40% over that same period.

Though FT reported that Starbucks has been working with advisors on a potential proposal, it remains unclear how serious the coffee giant is about its interest.

📸 : Getty / Starbucks / Chipotle

Jamie, pull that deal up again.⁣
⁣
Spotify and Joe Rogan are renewing their licensing agreement for Rogan’s chart-topping podcast. Neither side has disclosed terms of the multiyear deal, but the Wall Street Journal reported it’s similar to their last agreement, which was worth $250 million. In turn, Spotify maintains licensing rights and ad sales.⁣
⁣
Both parties have benefited from the partnership, which began in 2020. “The Joe Rogan Experience” was Spotify’s most-listened-to podcast last year, drawing more than 18 million followers, according to Edison Research.⁣
⁣
Jordan Newman, Spotify’s head of content partnerships, said, “Joe has built something incredibly enduring, and his show continues to resonate with a massive global audience because there’s simply nothing else like.”⁣
⁣

This USB Adapter Can Hack Your Network

This looks like a normal USB-C Ethernet adapter and hub, but inside is a Linux computer built for penetration testing.

Darren Kitchen from Hak5 shows me the new LAN Turtle Hub, which can provide remote access, sniff network traffic, intercept USB devices and even exfiltrate files, all while continuing to work like a normal Ethernet adapter.

The scary part? The user may have no idea anything is happening.

Use tools like this only on systems you own or have explicit permission to test.

A pilot believes he may have spotted the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane using Google Earth 👀✈️⁠
⁠
Justin Myers, who has nearly 25 years of flying experience, says he identified unusual shapes near Nikumaroro Island that closely match the size and structure of Earhart’s Lockheed Electra 10E 🤯⁠
⁠
After comparing measurements, he claims one object measured around 39 feet,the same length as parts of the aircraft, along with what he thinks could be debris like a fuselage section and even an engine 😮⁠
⁠
He said: “It looked man-made… it looked like a section of aircraft fuselage”⁠
⁠
Despite submitting his findings to authorities, no major investigations have been launched, and his theory remains unverified 👀⁠
⁠
He added: “What I can’t say is that is definitely Amelia’s Electra.”⁠
⁠
The disappearance of Earhart in 1937 remains one of aviation’s biggest mysteries, and for now, this is just the latest possible clue 😬
Just keep it away from the mouse...🤣
My dad works for rnicrosoft🤣

Encyclopaedia Britannica is coming for OpenAI. 📚⚖️⁠
⁠
Britannica and Merriam-Webster have filed a lawsuit in Manhattan federal court, alleging OpenAI copied their content without permission, including claims that ChatGPT can reproduce Britannica entries in near-verbatim form.⁠
⁠
The suit also claims the tech pulls users away from Britannica’s sites, because people get the info straight from the chatbot instead of clicking through to the original source.⁠
⁠
In other words, one of the oldest names in knowledge is accusing one of the newest giants in AI of building on its work, and this could get messy fast.

A Tennessee grandma says she spent nearly six months in jail after AI facial recognition wrongly linked her to a bank fraud case in North Dakota. 😳⁠
⁠
Angela Lipps, 50, says U.S. Marshals arrested her at gunpoint in July 2025 while she was babysitting, despite her saying she’d never even been to North Dakota.⁠
⁠
Reports say she was held in Tennessee for months before being extradited, and it wasn’t until a lawyer later produced bank records placing her around 1,200 miles away at the time of the crimes that the case unraveled,  with charges later dismissed.⁠
⁠
She says the mistake upended her life, and her case is now fueling fresh backlash over police relying on AI matches as if they’re proof.

Turns out Pokémon Go wasn’t just catching Pikachu, it was quietly building a massive real-world mapping dataset.⁠
⁠
Reports say Niantic trained its Visual Positioning System (VPS) on 30+ billion images captured through Pokémon Go-style scanning, and that tech is now being used to help delivery robots navigate in cities (especially where GPS is shaky).⁠
⁠
Niantic Spatial has officially confirmed a partnership with Coco Robotics, with VPS being deployed to improve robot localization and precision for autonomous delivery.⁠
⁠
So yeah… all those years of spinning PokéStops and scanning landmarks? Congrats: you may have helped teach a robot how to find your front door. 🐭📦

Norway just said “enough” to the ensh*tification of the internet!🛜🙌⁠
⁠
They’re doing it with a savage campaign that calls out how apps and services keep getting worse on purpose. 😬📱⁠
⁠
The Norwegian Consumer Council (Forbrukerrådet) launched a satirical video featuring an “enshittificator” whose job is literally to take things that work and make them worse, basically a walking metaphor for ads, paywalls, scammy feeds, and updates that magically break stuff after you buy it.⁠
⁠
They’ve also dropped a major report, “Breaking Free: Pathways to a fair technological future,” and joined forces with 70+ groups across Europe and the U.S. urging policymakers in 14 countries to clamp down on the business models behind it, arguing this isn’t inevitable, it’s a choice companies make (and governments allow).⁠
⁠
And yes, the term “enshittification” was coined by author Cory Doctorow, and Norway’s basically trying to turn it into a political problem, not just an online joke.

A brutal new reality check for job hunters: a report claims 75% of résumés never reach a human, getting filtered out by Applicant Tracking Systems before a recruiter even sees them. 😬⁠
⁠
It comes as the U.S. saw 1.17 million job cuts in 2025, the most since the pandemic, with the article arguing AI is now reshaping hiring into something totally different from the pre-Covid model.⁠
⁠
The piece says companies are rebuilding workflows around what AI is expected to do, even though Gartner reportedly found only 1 in 50 AI investments delivers transformational value. Meanwhile, McKinsey is cited saying AI fluency demands in job listings have surged.⁠
⁠
And it gets even wilder: the article points to the rise of automated applications, recruiter tools that scan your online footprint before they read a résumé, and even “AI twins” of candidates that can interact with employers first.⁠
⁠
The takeaway? Job searching is becoming as much about getting past systems, and proving AI literacy, as it is about your actual experience.

Researchers at Cybernews say an unprotected MongoDB database they believe is tied to IDMerit left roughly 1 billion sensitive records exposed across 26 countries, including more than 203 million in the U.S. alone.⁠
⁠
The database reportedly had no password, and included details like full names, home addresses, postal codes, dates of birth, national ID numbers, phone numbers, emails, and gender, the same kind of info used for identity checks.⁠
⁠
Cybernews says it was found on Nov. 11, 2025 and secured the next day, with no public evidence that the data was downloaded, though researchers warn exposed databases can be copied quickly.⁠
⁠
IDMerit denies a breach, saying it doesn’t “own, control or store customer data” and that its “systems and security infrastructure have never been compromised.”

Yu-Gi-Oh is distancing itself after the White House’s official X account used clips from the anime in a meme-style video.⁠
⁠
In March, the account posted a montage captioned “JUSTICE THE AMERICAN WAY” featuring clips from a bunch of franchises, including Yu-Gi-Oh, set to the iconic Mortal Kombat theme.⁠
⁠
But later, the official Yu-Gi-Oh account responded, saying it wasn’t involved and didn’t approve the footage being used.⁠
⁠
“It has come to our attention that a post on the White House’s official X account used footage from the anime series Yu-Gi-Oh,” they said in a statement.⁠
⁠
According to Yu-Gi-Oh, the White House used clips from the anime “without any authorization from the rights holder.”⁠
⁠
“Regarding this matter, no one associated with the manga or anime had any involvement, and no permission was granted for the use of this intellectual property,” they added.⁠
⁠
It’s not yet clear whether Konami will take legal action.

Some Hisense TV owners are claiming they’re being hit with intrusive ads when they do something as basic as changing channels, with pop-ups appearing like they’re part of the TV experience, not optional extras. 📺😬⁠
⁠
According to the complaints, the ads can feel unavoidable and disruptive, sparking backlash from people who say they already paid for the TV and shouldn’t be forced to watch marketing just to use it normally.⁠
⁠
To be clear, these are reported user complaints, but the bigger issue is the same one people keep raising with smart TVs: once your screen is connected, it can start behaving more like an ad platform than a product you own.

We’ve been getting a lot of questions lately about how the Internet Archive digitizes books.

The short answer: page by page, by hand, and without destroying the book.

You may remember Eliza Zhang, whose book-scanning video went viral in 2021, reaching 7.7 million people in its first 48 hours.

The video showed something that’s easy to miss: digitizing a book isn’t just a matter of putting it on a machine. Books can be fragile, irregular, full of fold-outs, and hundreds of years old. Our digitization staff carefully handle them while creating digital copies and preserving the originals.

We wrote the story behind that viral video in 2021. With renewed attention on how books are being digitized, it’s worth revisiting.

🔗 Read the story at the link in our bio.

Preservation is the remedy for cultural loss.⁠

Your AI just learned how you write. Paste an email, tell it to respond, and watch it match your exact style, short, polite, and ready to send in one click.

Gemini's new "Write Like Me" skill pulls samples from your sent box and locks in your openings, tone, sentence length, and closings. Then you call the skill in any new chat, drop in an email, add a one-line note like "decline this," and it drafts a reply that actually sounds like you.

If you ignore repetitive emails like I used to, this is the one skill to set up today.

Stop running your AI skills one at a time. Stack them. 🔗

Gemini lets you call multiple skills in a single prompt, so they handle a whole task together.

Example:
→ /proposal-writer builds a client proposal using real prices from an attached pricing sheet
→ /write-like-me drafts the email to the client in his own style

Remotion has a built-in skill called Remotion Maps. Feed it a prompt describing the route, the map style, and how the camera should move, and it renders a cinematic animation that follows the actual highways with smooth camera choreography.

Can Hyperframes match it?

DOTS turns AI into your project assistant. Ask it to create a workspace for any project, and it instantly generates notes, checklists, and sub-pages, all contextualized to what it knows about you.

One prompt: "create a new sub page in the scratch pad for a video I'm making about the launch of dots." Seconds later it had the page built out with notes, checklists, and links back to past chats on the topic.

If you've used Notion, Pages feels familiar, except your dot fills it in for you.

DOTS can run recurring tasks, triggers, and reminders. Example: "Tomorrow is OpenAI's Dev Day. Review the main keynote. As soon as it's finished, give me a summary of everything they launched." 

Scheduled tasks can fire from a form entry, an incoming email, a weekly cadence, or a one-off in the future, all routed straight to your dot.

Call DOTS on voice mode. Describe what you're hunting for. It browses the web, finds matching products, and sends the links straight to your chat while you're still on the call.

Test run: asked for magnetic wooden cairns like an art piece I'd seen. Mid-call it came back with hand-shaped walnut stones with hidden magnets, plus sapele and mixed wood sets, and dropped the four closest links into the thread.

Hands-free product research that actually finishes the task before you hang up.

One prompt. Three intros. A thumbnail. And motion graphics that sync perfectly to your script, all delivered at once. Dots just did your entire content setup.

The wild part: Dots delegated across Work and Codex on its own, prompting each skill with way more detail than you'd bother typing yourself.

> intro skill wrote 3 options in Work, picked the best
> Codex skill built motion graphics timed to the script
> thumbnail skill ran in a separate chat in parallel

One agent orchestrating multiple threads, multiple skills, one output.

Stop juggling ten different chats and work sessions. Meet DOTS, the always-on agent that orchestrates your entire ChatGPT from one central place.

It has access to your memories, connected tools, skills, and scheduled tasks. It can spin up new chats, work sessions, or codex sessions, even on your computer while it's on.

Plus it gets its own persistent cloud computer, and the chat follows you between phone and desktop. Rolling out on Pro and Enterprise first.

Can Humanizer make AI writing sound human?

You know the pattern: "it's not this, it's that." The "welcome to system one models" closer. That vague "essay vs. decision" setup. Cloud's default tweets are covered in it.

Install the Humanizer skill, run your draft through it, and it reworks the slop lines into something that actually sounds like a person wrote it. Especially useful on longer writing than tweets.

Your AI designs look generic? Impeccable fixes that with 24 commands that amplify boring layouts, inject real motion, and kill the AI tells your users already spot.

Watch one "bolder" command turn a flat Utah National Parks site into something with stronger typography, deep forest green sections, and larger imagery. Then "delight" adds a stamp-press animation when you check off a park. Then "critique" runs a full design + responsiveness review with fixes you can actually ship.

The easiest way I've found to level up AI-generated designs.

Ubuntu 26.10 is making a major change to how Secure Boot handles the boot process.

Canonical’s signed GRUB build will no longer support /boot on Btrfs, XFS, ZFS, LVM, LUKS, or software RAID (except RAID1) when Secure Boot is enabled. Support for HFS+, Apple partition tables, and JPEG/PNG image loading is also being removed.

The goal is security. GRUB runs early in the boot chain, and its filesystem parsers have been involved in Secure Boot vulnerabilities. By reducing the number of parsers and features available before the kernel loads, Canonical aims to reduce the attack surface.

This does not mean Btrfs, ZFS, LVM, or LUKS are being removed from Ubuntu. They continue to work after the system has booted.

Most users should not be affected, as the standard Ubuntu installer uses a Secure Boot-friendly /boot setup. However, users with customized boot configurations should check their setup before upgrading to Ubuntu 26.10.

If you need the full GRUB feature set with Secure Boot, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS remains an option.

Linus Torvalds being an absolute gigachad! 😎🔥

The Steam Deck could get a serious memory performance boost from a new Linux technology called CRAM.

Developed by Gregory Price and his team at Meta, CRAM takes a different approach to memory compression. Unlike ZRAM and zswap, which work through the swap layer, CRAM keeps compressed data directly in RAM and lets Linux manage it using standard memory semantics.

The goal is to reduce the overhead caused by page faults and swap behavior. In read-only testing, CRAM reached up to 489 million operations per second, compared with around 1.1 million for ZRAM, delivering a reported 452× speedup.

Write-heavy workloads see much smaller gains, but a test with 20% writes still showed a 5.4× speedup.

CRAM is still experimental, with memory allocation and compression-ratio challenges to solve. If it eventually reaches the Linux kernel, it could benefit everything from large servers to memory-constrained devices like the Steam Deck.

Another 12 security vulnerabilities have been disclosed in both X.Org Server and XWayland, with TrendAI Zero Day Initiative identifying the issues with assistance from AI.

The vulnerabilities include use-after-free bugs, heap buffer overflows, out-of-bounds reads and writes, and numeric truncation issues affecting components such as XKB, XInput, GLX, RandR, XFixes, and Glamor.

The issues affect versions before xorg-server 21.1.25 and xwayland 24.1.14.

Users running affected versions should update to the latest available releases to get the security fixes.

Thank you @lewishamilton for visiting @perplexity and spending time with us. Wishing you the best for the rest of the season. The race is still on!

Congrats Tim on an incredible journey at Apple. Few people have ever shipped at that scale without letting the bar for excellence slip. You’ve raised the standard for all of us to aspire to; thanks for everything.

“Our broader vision is to make the planet smarter,” says UC Berkeley alum and @perplexity co-founder, CEO, and president @aravindsrinivas (PhD ’21, Computer Science).

Srinivas’ AI journey began at the Indian Institute of Technology, teaching computers to play games like Pong and Breakout. That early spark led him into deeper machine learning research, eventually taking him to the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms. Srinivas then set his sights on Berkeley.

“When it came to AI, Berkeley was the most happening university at the time,” he recalls. He was inspired by EECS professor and co-director of UC Berkeley’s AI Research Lab Pieter Abbeel and the students in his lab.

“From them, I learned that software engineering is critical to doing great work in AI,” he says. “It’s not just about mathematical equations on a whiteboard, but rather making them work in practice. So you need to be a good engineer.”

In 2022, Srinivas co-founded Perplexity with the goal of powering curiosity with answers backed by up-to-date sources. “PhD students write papers, and for every sentence they write, they reference another paper. We baked that principle into an AI chatbot, and that ended up becoming Perplexity.”

Since launch, the platform has attracted millions of users looking for clear, credible information. As Srinivas notes, “With Perplexity, we had a vision for creating a completely new search experience, where you’re now able to ask questions that you otherwise would not have been able to ask before.”

His advice for anyone building something new? “A true vision about something can be seen by other people, too. But the most important part — and the hardest — is to persist through the phase where you’re not sure. Never give up, just keep at it”.

We are fortunate to live at an incredible moment in history. In the next few years, people will be able to use superintelligence beyond human capacity to create and discover extraordinary new things, build new businesses, express our ideas, learn new concepts, and improve our lives, health, relationships and careers, writes @zuck.

The defining question of our age isn’t whether superintelligence will exist, but who will have access to it. Will it be centralized and restricted to a few institutions, or will it be a tool that empowers everyone?

I propose a philosophy based on individual empowerment as the source of prosperity, invention as the primary purpose of superintelligence, and balance of power as the foundation of safety.

The notion that AI is so dangerous that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power seems dangerous. Putting power in people’s hands to pursue their own aspirations is how humanity has made the most progress. Invention, not automation, will be the greatest contribution of superintelligence.

As intelligence becomes abundant, the most important question will be how we direct it. Rather than centralizing this power, we believe that delivering personal superintelligence to everyone is the way to answer this question. Meta is committed to building with the principles of individual empowerment, invention and balance of power.

The arc of human history has bent toward putting more power in people’s hands. If these values lead the way, then I am optimistic that we can build a positive future for everyone.

One of the biggest surprises in AI over the last few years has been how well coding agents generalize beyond software. 

In a recent essay, MIT professor Philip Isola argued that we may be entering the era of robot-use agents: general-purpose models that can control different robots, write policies, and learn new physical tasks with little or no robot-specific training.

In this episode of Decoded, we're joined by the founders of Waddle Labs and RoboCurve, two of the startups whose work helped drive this realization. They're working at the frontier of using general-purpose models to control robots, and their recent demos helped inspire the growing conversation around robot-use agents. 

Together, we dig into the research behind that idea, from code-as-policies and vision-language-action models to the harnesses and evals needed to make these systems work in the real world.

🤖 Tune in on our YouTube or at the link in bio!

Hop Aero is building rockets that can deliver cargo anywhere on Earth in minutes.

They’re starting with military logistics and other time-sensitive payloads, including temperature-controlled materials with short shelf lives, where getting something there much faster can materially change the outcome.

They’ve already built and successfully hot-fired a new rocket engine, and signed $1.37B in commercial LOIs.

A lot of construction work is still done by hand simply because the machines to automate it don’t exist. That’s become a bottleneck for building things like solar farms, data centers, and other critical infrastructure.

Cosmic Robotics is building those machines. Their robots have already installed 11,000 solar panels, and they just signed a major contract with the largest construction company in the country.

They’re building the construction robots we’ll need on Earth today, and eventually on the Moon and Mars.

Attack drones are reshaping modern warfare, but many countries still lack an effective way to defend their airspace.

Earendil Robotics is building autonomous interceptors, along with the software and training needed to stand up that capability from scratch. Their systems can take off, transit, and intercept targets on their own, reducing months of pilot training to a few clicks.

The goal is air defense that’s affordable enough to deploy in large numbers and simple enough to operate at scale.

Protein in hot coffee = absolutely fine

Heat can denature whey protein, which simply means the protein unfolds and changes shape. It does not mean the protein has been destroyed or that the amino acids in it have suddenly disappeared.

In fact, this happens to protein every time we cook eggs, chicken, salmon, or any other protein-rich food. 

Plus, your digestive system also denatures protein as part of the normal digestion process before breaking it down further and absorbing the amino acids.

And yes, with extreme temperatures combined with prolonged heating, proteins can eventually undergo changes that affect nutritional quality. But adding whey isolate to a normal cup of hot coffee is nowhere near that kind of heat exposure.

The bigger issue with most protein powders in hot coffee isn’t the nutrition, it’s the texture. Chalkiness, grit, weird aftertaste…

That’s exactly why I chose a cold cross-flow microfiltrated protein: the perfect texture, no aftertaste, blends beautifully into coffee, tea, matcha, yogurt and more.

One little tip though: make your coffee or tea first, then add the protein powder on top and mix it in. If you pour boiling water directly over it that sudden hit of boiling liquid can make whey clump.

بعضی سفرها وقتی تموم میشن تازه شروع میشن، تازه تجربیات و روایت های اون سفر میشینه تو افکار و زندگیت.
اینجا یه گوشه از ایرانه که کل مردم روستا پارچه چادر شب بافی تولید میکنن. روستای قاسم آباد در گیلان مرجع این هنر و میزبان مردم هنرمند این منطقه ست.

در فصل دوم مجموعه مستند ایران من، به صنایع دستی شاخص سراسر ایران پرداختیم که به زودی در پلتفرم فیلیمو میتونید تماشا کنید.

به وقت ۳۴ سالگی🍁

امروز داشتم پست های سالروز های تولدم رو تو آرشیو نگاه میکردم، دیدم سال به سال جملات و کلماتم کوتاه تر شده.
اینبار و امسال هم کوتاه تره،
همین رو اشاره کنم چند سالی میشه که روزهای تولدم رو تو سفر هستم و خوشحال از این بابت که مسیرم به سفر گره خورد و عمیق و عمیق تر تربیت شدم در مسیر کمال. 
بزرگی میگفت شرط رسیدن به کمال، جدایی از اکنونه و هر جدایی ای به کمال نمیرسه. به نوع نگاه ما و شهودی بودنمون بستگی داره و اینکه کمال چیه و کی تعریفش کرده هم نمیدونیم. شاید به مسیر رسیدن به کمال میگن کمال و شاید مقصدی نباشه و همین مسیر باشه که تجربه زیستن انسان رو چند برابر میکنه.

شاید اگه تناسخی وجود داشته باشه، اگه حق انتخابی باشه، ترجیح بدم اینسری اصفهان یا شیراز بدنیا بیام، شاید در دهه سی یا چهل.
شما چطور؟

اینجا بزرگترین کاروانسرای سرپوشیده ای ایران.
بازار سعدالسلطنه قزوین

بارها گفتم همین‌ امارات دنبال یه وجب دیوار تاریخی میگرده که به خودش و سرزمینش هویت بده.
در مقابلش در ایران وجب به وجب تاریخ و بناهای تاریخی داریم.
و اتفاقا چون زیاد داریم، قدردانش نیستیم و متاسفانه بخش زیادیشون یا آسیب دیدن یا در معرض آسیب هستن یا رها شدن.
و اتفاقا چون در دوران دبستان و راهنمایی و دبیرستان حتی یک خط در کتاب های درسی توضیح داده نشده که چگونه باید حافظ میراث تاریخی و هویتی یک سرزمین باشیم، متاسفانه فرهنگ نگهداری در بین ما شکل نگرفته و برعکس فکر میکنیم با یادگاری نوشتن میتونیم اثری به اون بنا اضافه کنیم.

⁨	به قول هوشنگ سیحون که میگفت اسلام معماری نداشت، هنر نداشت. وقتی اعراب به ایران هجوم اوردن و کاخ ها و چهار باغ ها رو دیدن گفتن اینجا همون بهشتیه که پیامبر وعده داده بود.و بعد از تسلطشون بر ایران، معماران ایرانی آتشکده ها رو به مساجد تبدیل کردن و هنرشون رو در بناهای ایرانی در دوران اسلامی به کار بردن.⁩
ماجرای ساعت آفتابی محله جلفای اصفهان

یه سوالی هست که اخیرا از اطرافیانم میپرسم،
اگر ایرانی نبودی، دلت میخواست ایرانی باشی؟

قدیمیا میگفتن زندگی کردن، هنر میخواد
ما میگفتیم چه هنری، زندگی در جریانه و ماهم باهاش پیش میریم دیگه.
اما وقتی با گذشت سن، تجربیاتمون بیشتر میشه، میفهمیم چه کاش ها و چه حسرت هایی رو پشت سر گذاشتیم، چه روزهایی رو پشت سر گذروندیم و فکر میکردیم میگذره، اما سالها بعد عین بغض دست گذاشت رو گلوی ما.
با هر تصمیم و با هر اتفاق، چه چین و چروک هایی که بر پیشونی ما نقش بست و به ما یادآوری کرد که بله، زندگی کردن هنر میخواد.

Here’s the holy grail of investing: Find 15 good, uncorrelated return streams.

If you look at the math of diversification, getting out to 15 uncorrelated streams allows you to reduce about 80% of your risk without reducing your return. That increases your return-to-risk ratio by a factor of five—giving you the upside without the downside.

Credit: Sam Parr, Shaan Puri, and My First Million

#RayDalio #Investing #Diversification #FinancialWisdom

In order to be successful, you have to do five things. There’s a sequence to it.

1. Have (audacious) goals.
2. Identify and don’t tolerate problems.
3. Diagnose the problems to get at their root causes.
4. Design a path to fix those things.
5. Push through to results.

This is what I call looping. Go for your goals, identify your problems, get to the root cause, design a path, and push through. Life is basically just doing that over and over again. If you do that, you’ll make the advances.

#Principles #RayDalio  #PersonalGrowth

Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle.

Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble.

So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle.
#RayDalio #Economy #LongTermDebtCycle #Finance

Thinking about problems that are difficult to solve may make you anxious, but not thinking about them (and hence not dealing with them) should make you more anxious still. When a problem stems from your own lack of talent or skill, most people feel shame.

Get over it. I cannot emphasize this enough: Acknowledging your weaknesses is not the same as surrendering to them. #principleoftheday

"My number one principle would be pain plus reflection equals progress."

At #MIGlobal Asia Summit 2026 today, Ray Dalio, Founder, Bridgewater Associates; Chairman, Dalio Family Office, provided numerous nuggets of wisdom during a conversation with Toto Wolff.

Watch all session replays: https://milkeninstitute.org/events/asia-summit-2026/program

#AsiaSummit #Asia #RayDalio #BridgewaterAssociates

Everyone makes mistakes. 

The main difference is that successful people learn from them and unsuccessful people don’t. 

By creating an environment in which it is okay to safely make mistakes so that people can learn from them, you’ll see rapid progress and fewer significant mistakes. This is especially true in organizations where creativity and independent thinking are important, as success will inevitably require the acceptance of failure as a part of the process. 

As Thomas Edison once said, “I have not failed. I’ve just found ten thousand ways that do not work.” #principleoftheday

Though it won't feel that way at first, each and every problem you encounter is an opportunity; for that reason, it is essential that you bring them to the surface. 

Most people don't like to do this, especially if it exposes their own weaknesses or the weaknesses of someone they care about, but successful people know they have to. #principleoftheday

Worrying about "blame" and "credit" or "positive" and "negative" feedback impedes the iterative process that is essential to learning. 

Remember that what has already happened lies in the past and no longer matters except as a lesson for the future. #principleoftheday

The holy grail of investing is knowing how to balance.

When you can take equally good things where your expectation of return is equal, but because they are uncorrelated and move differently, they balance each other. That is how you can reduce your risk without reducing your returns.

You have to understand that the market is a zero-sum game. The consensus is already reflected in the price, and trying to beat it is a difficult game. In fact, it is more difficult to compete and be successful in the markets than it is to compete in the Olympics. We must be humble about that.

But achieving that balance so you can get a good return without losing a lot of money is everything. Most of my own money is invested in exactly that.
#Investing #AssetAllocation #RiskManagement #Principles

This is a requirement.

Being considerate means allowing other people to mostly do what they want, so long as it is consistent with our principles, policies, and the law. It also means being willing to put others ahead of your own desires. If the people on both sides of an argument approach their disagreements in this way, we will have many fewer disputes about who is offending whom. #principleoftheday
You need to develop a fierce intolerance of badness of any kind, regardless of its severity. #principleoftheday
They are rare. Such relationships take time to build and can only be built if you treat such people well. #principleoftheday

Before SpongeBob SquarePants became one of the most beloved cartoons of all time, it started with a few sketches and a marine biologist's imagination.

Stephen Hillenburg combined his love of ocean life with animation to create Bikini Bottom and its unforgettable characters. His early concepts already featured the humor, personality, and underwater world that millions of fans would eventually fall in love with.

The show premiered in 1999, and Hillenburg passed away in 2018 at age 57. More than two decades after its debut, his creation continues to entertain generations around the world.

NFL legend Mike Ditka has passed away at 86. 🕊️🏈
“Iron Mike” leaves behind a legacy few in football history can match. Ditka helped redefine the tight end position, became the first tight end to record a 1,000-yard season, earned five Pro Bowl selections, won championships with the Bears and Cowboys as a player, and later returned to Chicago to lead the iconic 1985 Bears to victory in Super Bowl XX.

He was a two-time NFL Coach of the Year, a member of both the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame, and had his No. 89 retired by the Bears.

More than the trophies and accolades, Ditka became inseparable from the identity of Chicago football remembered for his toughness, passion, larger-than-life personality, and love for the game. An icon whose impact stretched far beyond the sidelines, he will be deeply missed by generations of football fans. ❤️

Rest in peace, Coach. 🕊️

In 2021, he was found dead in a Spanish prison, just hours after a court approved his extradition to the United States. His death was officially ruled a suicide, although his family disputed that conclusion.

His story is so unusual that some of the claims surrounding it still need to be separated from what actually happened.

🔹️ فرآیند ارزیابی و داوری آنلاین رویداد ملی صنایع خلاق «مانوین ۱۴۰۵» با بررسی ۴۸۷ شرکت به پایان رسید و حالا ۱۴۰ شرکت برگزیده در مسیر کلینیک رشد و منتورینگ آثار قرار دارند.

📊 نگاهی به مسیر طی‌شده:

▪️ ۴۹۵ پرونده ثبت‌شده
▪️ ۴۸۷ شرکت وارد داوری تخصصی آنلاین
▪️ ۱۴۰ شرکت منتخب کلینیک رشد
▪️ حدود ۹۰ جلسه منتورینگ برگزارشده
▪️ ۵ اتاق تخصصی برای رشد و آماده‌سازی آثار
▪️ هدف نهایی: آماده‌سازی ۷۰ ارائه برتر برای رقابت روی صحنه مانوین در اصفهان

🔸️ در داوری آنلاین، طرح‌ها بر اساس شاخص‌هایی همچون اثرگذاری فرهنگی و اجتماعی، نوآوری، تجاری‌سازی، توسعه بازار، ظرفیت صادرات و توان تیمی ارزیابی شدند.

📽 ویدیو نشست اعضای شورای سردبیری «مانوین»

معاون وزارت کار: صنایع خلاق باید از حمایت‌های مقطعی عبور کنند

سید مالک حسینی در نشست هم‌اندیشی مشارکت صنایع خلاق بزرگ در رویداد ملی «مانوین» بر ضرورت شکل‌گیری زیست‌بوم اقتصادی پایدار و اتصال ظرفیت‌های مالی و بازار تأکید کرد.

به گزارش روابط عمومی مانوین، نشست هم‌اندیشی مشارکت صنایع خلاق بزرگ در رویداد ملی صنایع خلاق «مانوین» با حضور عبدالحسن بهرامی، رئیس مرکز راهبری ستادهای توسعه اقتصاد دانش‌بنیان معاونت علمی، فناوری و اقتصاد دانش‌بنیان ریاست‌جمهوری، سید مالک حسینی، معاون توسعه کارآفرینی و اشتغال وزارت تعاون، کار و رفاه اجتماعی، و جمعی از فعالان، شرکت‌ها و ذی‌نفعان حوزه صنایع خلاق برگزار شد.

سید مالک حسینی در این نشست با تأکید بر ضرورت اقتصادی‌شدن صنایع خلاق، شکل‌گیری یک زیست‌بوم پایدار و بازتعریف نقش دولت در حمایت از این حوزه را از الزامات توسعه صنایع خلاق دانست.

وی اظهار کرد: اگر صنایع خلاق نتوانند به یک فعالیت اقتصادی پایدار تبدیل شوند، باید نگاه ما به نحوه حمایت و توسعه این حوزه تغییر کند. دولت باید در بخش‌هایی که نیاز به حمایت وجود دارد نقش‌آفرینی کند، اما در بخش‌هایی نیز از تصدی‌گری فاصله بگیرد و موانع پیش روی فعالان اقتصادی را برطرف کند.معاون توسعه کارآفرینی و اشتغال وزارت تعاون، کار و رفاه اجتماعی افزود: فعالان صنایع خلاق باید مشخص کنند دولت در چه حوزه‌هایی حضور داشته باشد
📸 گزارش تصویری نشست اعضای شورای سردبیری «مانوین»

تفاهم‌نامه همکاری برای اجرای طرح ملی «جوانه خلاق» با هدف حمایت از کارآفرینی جوانان از مسیر توسعه کسب‌وکارهای خلاق، میان مرکز راهبری ستادهای توسعه اقتصاد دانش‌بنیان معاونت علمی و معاونت توسعه کارآفرینی و اشتغال وزارت تعاون، کار و رفاه اجتماعی به امضا رسید.

🔸بر اساس این توافق، شناسایی و تسهیل دسترسی جوانان دارای ایده‌ها و طرح‌های خلاق و نوآور به تسهیلات اشتغال‌زایی، یکی از محورهای اصلی همکاری دو طرف خواهد بود و کسب‌وکارهای فعال در حوزه صنایع خلاق نیز در دریافت تسهیلات تکلیفی اشتغال در اولویت قرار می‌گیرند.

🔹شناسایی، توانمندسازی و حمایت مالی از جوانان دارای ایده‌های خلاق و نوآور، حمایت از کارآفرینی و تجاری‌سازی محصولات صنایع خلاق با محوریت بخش خصوصی و تسهیل بهره‌مندی کسب‌وکارها و مشاغل فعال در حوزه صنایع خلاق و نوآور، از دیگر محورهای این تفاهم‌نامه است.

🔸مطابق تفاهم‌نامه، مجموع منابع مالی اختصاص‌یافته برای اجرای طرح «جوانه خلاق» ۳ هزار میلیارد ریال تعیین شده است.

The tech in the Vegas Sphere is mindblowing...

And it turns out, the screen (biggest ever created), is the least impressive part of the venue.

The most impressive part, is the audio...it’s the most advanced sound system ever built.

Inside the Sphere, there are 167,000 speakers hidden behind the screen.

That’s 8 speakers per person.

And this allows them to use Beam Forming technology to produce custom sound for each seat.

This means they could play music in English for one section and music in Spanish for another section at the same time.

Completely personalized sound...pretty nuts!

The other thing that blew me away was the visuals.

Not the screen specifically, moreso the camera.

Turns out, the Sphere is so massive with such an extreme curvature, they had to invent the world’s most powerful video camera just to film for it.

They call it, The Big Sky.

It has a 165 degree field of view and shoots in 18K.

1 second of footage takes up 60GB of storage.

They even had to build a secret mini sphere in California just to have somewhere to test how footage would look before it went into production.

Overall, the project cost $2.3B and zero expense was spared.

The second Sphere is under contract for Abu Dhabi and set to begin next year...I bet we see 10 of these by 2035.

Also, shoutout to YouTube channels Megabuilds and Jacob Owen for making these insane visuals.

This is the most insane tech company in the world...ASML.

Every single computer chip on Earth is made using their machines.

Nvidia, Apple, Intel, Samsung…none of them can make any chips without ASML.

But here’s the craziest part, the way these machines work is completely mindblowing.

This is how computer chips are actually made…

First, the ASML machine fires tiny droplets of molten tin.

50,000 droplets per second…each one thinner than a human hair.

They then shoot a laser at each individual droplet, which vaporizes the tin into a plasma.

That plasma…is hotter than the surface of the sun.

It’s so hot, that when the plasma is created, it also emits extreme UV light.

The ASML machine guides that light through a series of hyper precise mirrors to beam it on a stencil which has the pattern for the chip.

That pattern is then projected onto a thin slice of silicon that’s coated with special light reactive chemicals…essentially using the light to print the pattern onto the silicon.

The machine then repeats this light printing process thousands of times, to build layer upon layer of silicon that stacks together to create a fully functional chip.

Now here’s where it gets wild…

These chip designs are super intricate…billions of transistors spaced only a few atoms apart.

And that means the accuracy of the ASML machines are the equivalent of shooting a laser from the moon and hitting a penny on Earth.

How insane is that?

So in layman’s terms, the process to make a computer chip is vaporizing molten tin to create invisible light that beams atomic patterns onto thousands of layers of silicon.

Shoutout science.

DoorDash is completely reinventing the food delivery space.

And I don’t think people realize what they’re actually doing under the hood.

Last week they announced a ton of new features at their annual event.

The biggest one, to me, was their ultraquiet food delivery drone, DoorDash Air.

This thing can fly straight from the restaurant to your yard, overtop of all the traffic and dramatically reduces delivery times.

But it turns out, the drone program is only a small piece of their master plan.

I sat down with Stanley Tang, one of the original Co-Founders and Head of Labs at DoorDash.

He was the mastermind behind Air and runs their R&D Labs.

And what he said really surprised me…

The secret sauce at DoorDash isn’t just the drones…it’s the entire delivery operating system layer they’ve built to sit underneath.

DoorDash now has lots of different ways to deliver your food.

They’ve got Dashers, the human drivers, Dot, the autonomous robots, and now Air, the drone fleet.

When an order comes in, they’re able to intelligently route and deliver it in the fastest and most cost efficient way possible.

As they build more and more methods for delivery, including things like drones and other autonomous vehicles, this will increase their ability to serve customers. 

That orchestration layer underneath is the secret sauce behind why they’re so effective.

Stanley also broke down how they’re planning to use AI in their new Text Doordash feature as well as how he runs the R&D Lab to come up with new breakthroughs.

And it’s clear they are doing everything they can to pioneer the future of delivery.
