This Japanese broccoli farmer figured out how to automate his farm with AI

His name is Hiroki Tomayasu.

And even though he was never taught how to drive tractors or grow vegetables…

He’s built an entire software system to digitize his farm, all without knowing how to code.

For example…

Hiroki wanted to find a way to automate his fieldwork.

But typically, self-driving tractors like these (https://carbonrobotics.com/carbon-autonomy) are super expensive. 

So instead, he figured out how to build a GPS auto-steer system, that drives his tractor for him, at a fraction of the cost.

He’s also built bots to automate his greenhouse, software for tracking his plant logs,

He’s even using satellite imagery analysis to figure out exactly which crops and fields are performing the best.

And this is all powered by ChatGPT and Codex that he works with every single day.

Hiroki describes using AI like getting access to an ultra-talented engineer that is always by his side.

And the coolest part about this story is that he’s live documenting all of his AI farm experiments on this website (https://note.com/tomiyasu16)

That includes his learnings, what he’s building, and step by step tutorials for other farmers if they want to try it for themselves.

These are my favorite types of AI stories cause it really shows how inventive people can be when they get access to world class tools.

OpenAI has officially launched dots.

And this is a massive deal because dots are a completely different category of AI product. 

dots are always-on agents inside of ChatGPT that handle ongoing work.

Each dot has its own cloud computer and browser, which means they can keep working on tasks continuously while you’re away.

Now the big question on everyone’s mind.…is how dots are different from the normal ChatGPT and Codex experiences.

Think of it like this…

ChatGPT and Codex are more reactive.

You ask them questions or give them a task…and they answer to the best of their ability.

So it’s kinda like you’re driving the car and they are the engine. The car doesn’t move unless you push the pedal down.

Dots, on the other hand, are completely different.

They’re designed to be more proactive.

All you have to do is give them an initial objective, set boundaries, and let them cook.

They’ll come back when they need you to weigh in or review important decisions.

So it’s more like you get in the backseat of the car, say where you want to go, and your dot can drive, steer, and fill up its own gas tank.

Now the biggest reason why dots are so compelling, is that they’re powered by GPT-6 Astra.

Essentially, their agent brain is genius level with one of the best models in the world, which means their capacity to do things is extremely advanced.

This is the way most people envisioned working with AI, and it’s now available.

DoorDash just officially launched their drone delivery program.

It’s called DoorDash Air.

And this is going to completely change how food gets delivered in the future.

Customers can now place orders that fly straight from the restaurant and land directly in your yard.

Now the big perk is that these drones can fly over top of the traffic, so on average, order flight time is just 5 minutes.

These drones are extremely quiet and you can actually watch the drone’s route via a flyover visualization as it gets delivered.

The service is just starting to roll out in select markets (“in the coming months”) with companies like Chipotle and Popeyes, but this is a peek into the future of cutting edge logistics and delivery.

Now in addition to drones, DoorDash also announced several new AI features that make ordering much more personalized and dynamic.

The biggest one is called Text DoorDash.

This allows you to have a text conversation directly with DoorDash to order your food.

You could say something like, “My mom is in town this weekend. She loves pasta, but doesn’t like seafood. Order us dinner for Saturday night.”

DoorDash now has a personalized AI memory layer that knows exactly where you live and what you like based on past order history, and all the restaurants available to you at that moment.

It can automatically find the perfect meal, list it out for you, and place the order instantly.

This same approach now can be used for ordering groceries and even group dinners…simple text descriptions in, orders ready to go in seconds.

And it all works so well because of the new agentic ordering layer they’re rolling out.

All of this and a bunch of other updates were just announced at their Dash Forward event.

And this is going to completely change the way delivery works in the future.

#tech #ai #doordashpartner #food #drones @doordash

This factory in China designed robots that build each other

This is the latest project by UBTECH in China and its basically one giant industrial humanoid factory.

This factory in China is building a new robot every ten minutes.

On the floor, humanoid robots load parts and move materials.

Giant robot arms spin to assemble more than two thousand screws into each finished unit.

Automated vehicles and unmanned forklifts haul everything around.

The whole place sits on about two and a half football fields of factory floor.

And it works like a car plant…except the finished products get to walk out when they’re done.

But here’s the wild part…

These particular robots never have to stop working.

Instead of having to charge like most humanoids…

These guys have 2 battery packs in their back.

When one is running low, the robot walks over to the charging station, twists its torso, and pulls the dead battery out of its own back to hotswap.

3 minutes, no human involved.

That means the factory can run 24 hours per day without needing rest or breaks.
I’m telling you, robots building robots used to be something out of a sci-fi movie

Now it’s a literal production line in China with a quota attached.

It seems crazy now, but in a few years, this kind of production will be normalized around the globe

Google Gemini just integrated their agentic capabilities in Gemini Live.

And there’s a way of using this, not many people have tried yet, that is insanely valuable for creators and marketers.

With this integration, you now have voice control over your personal AI agent.

It can access Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Gmail, and even YouTube.

As a creator, I used this new update to build out an entire content pipeline for brand partnerships.

All I had to do was open Gemini Live and verbally describe the workflow I wanted.

And it built this whole thing out for me automatically.

First, it scans my email daily looking for any communication with brands for upcoming partnerships.

When it finds one, it extracts all of the campaign information shared by the brand…and searches all of my best content across Instagram and YouTube to better understand the narratives that have worked well for similar stories in the past.

Then, it uses all that info to automatically build out a new folder in Google Drive and creates a Doc inside it specifically for that campaign with ideas, power phrases, and formats that worked previously.

When I go to make the video, I just open that doc and I already have my notes in there ready to go.

I call this flow data-enabled creativity.

It’s using the data and examples from previous winning videos to help aim my creativity for the new campaign.

Now this is just a single creator workflow.

There are dozens of others you can run.

For example, I asked Gemini to build out an invoice tracking pipeline to keep track of any brand partnerships payments.

I also built an idea repurposer that consistently scans my Google Drive for old script documents and notes that can be repurposed into new content.

And the reason these are so easy to build is because of the voice capabilities in Gemini Live.

This flow is now available for Pro and Ultra users.

This company built a data center floating in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.

They’re called Panthalassa.

And they might be pioneering a whole new category of technology  See, a data center is really just thousands of chips that need two things… electricity to think, and water to stay cool.

On land, they compete with actual towns for both resources, which is why new ones keep getting blocked.

But the ocean has no towns, no permits, and no grid to strain.

Of course… there is just one problem.

They also have no place to plug in for electricity

So this floating datacenter was designed to make its own power.

Here’s how it works.

Picture a giant lollipop floating in the sea, with a round buoy on top and a long tube hanging straight down.

Waves only move on the surface of the ocean, so deep down, the water barely moves at all.

And that means the buoy rides up and down… while the tube stays still.

So every wave squeezes seawater through a turbine inside.

Think of it like a bike pump, except the ocean is the one pushing the handle. 

That same seawater generating electricity also cools the chips… so the ocean covers both critical resources.

Now you’d think calm weather would prevent this thing from running…

But the ocean works more like a battery.

The sun heats the air… the air makes wind… and the wind makes waves.

And they keep rolling long after the breeze is gone.

So it’s solar power… that also works at night.

Okay one more problem…how does all that power get back to land?

It doesn’t.

These things have no anchor, no fuel… and no cable to shore.

Instead, your AI query goes up to a satellite… and down to a buoy in the ocean.

For nearly three decades, Crucial has been more than just a brand - it’s been a trusted companion for millions of people building, upgrading, and creating. Thanks to an incredible community of passionate customers, dedicated partners, and talented Micron team members, Crucial became synonymous with innovation, quality, and reliability in memory and storage. We are deeply grateful for the support and loyalty that made this journey possible.⁣
 ⁣
Some things to note as we wind down:⁣
Crucial consumer products will continue to ship through the end of February 2026, and we’ll work closely with our partners and customers to ensure a smooth transition. Warranty service and support will remain available for all Crucial products. While this chapter is closing, Micron will continue to serve commercial customers globally with Micron-branded enterprise products.⁣

Thank you - for 29 amazing years of trust, collaboration, and shared success. Crucial wouldn’t have been what it was without you.⁣

🐉 Kung Fu Tuesdays 
‘Footwork – Quick Retreat’:

🐉👣The footwork for the quick retreat or rapid backward movement is similar to the quick advance, except you move in the opposite direction. From the on-guard position, move your front foot back. The front foot, like the quick advance, initiates the movement with the rear foot following just a split second later. Unless you move your rear foot before the front foot makes contact, the front foot cannot be planted properly. Unlike the quick advance, you do not have to slide your foot three inches. It is just one quick motion, but your body should be in alignment and in balance. If you were to move just once, you should be at the on-guard position when both of your feet are in place. But the purpose of this movement is to move your body four feet or more.

#brucelee #kungfutuesdays #gungfutuesdays #jkd #jeetkunedo #footwork #martialartists #martialarts

🐉🤜🏽💥 Kung Fu Tuesdays: ‘Fundamentals of Attacking’

💥It is easy to learn the mechanics of an attack, but to apply that attack in time with the opponent and at the correct distance takes a lot of practice. In attacking you must never be half-hearted. Your main concern is with the correct and most determined execution of your offensive. Every attack you make should be penetrating, disturbing your opponent’s rhythm and bringing pressure upon his morale. Remember though that your hands are not a hatchet to chop your opponent down. Rather, they are keys to unlock your opponent’s defense, and a different lock requires a different key. Thus, in order for an attack to be successful requires this ‘fitting in’ with the opponent. To attack correctly you must have a keen sense of timing with the opponent, a good judgment of distance between you and him, and the right application of speed and rhythm with the reactions of your adversary!

#BruceLee #KungFuTuesdays #GungFuTuesdays #FundamentalsOfAttacking #JeetKuneDo #jkd #martialarts #martialartist #chucknorris

🐉 Gung Fu Tuesdays: ‘Leading Finger Jab*’:

The leading finger jab is a good defensive counterattack weapon for stopping and attack before it unfolds, and as a consequence, it frustrates your opponent. It is easy to employ and is so quick that the opponent gets it in his eye before he can deliver his punch. It is thrown with your fingers outstretched, lengthening the extension of your hand. It is a good stop-hit weapon, and you should use it at every opportunity during the course of fighting. It enables you not only to score effectively and create openings but can also quickly subdue an aggressive opponent.
*always make sure to utilize protective gear when practicing the finger jab with a partner; never strike anyone in the eye except under extreme defensive circumstances.

🐉 Kung Fu Tuesdays: ‘Footwork -The Shuffle Step’:

To advance, do not cross or hop, but shuffle your feet. At the outset you will feel clumsy and slow, but as you keep practicing this movement daily, you will develop your speed and grace. To do the forward shuffle, stand in the on-guard position. To move forward, slide your front foot forward about a half step, widening the space between your feet just for a second as you slide your rear foot forward. When the rear foot is moved forward, you should be at the original position.
Keep your knees slightly bent and relaxed. The front foot is flat but not heavily planted on the floor. It should be light and raise intuitively on a quick movement or sudden shift of the body. The rear heel is almost always raised. The raised rear heel facilitates switching your weight immediately to the other foot when delivering a punch and allows fast reaction of that foot. Naturally the heel should drop at the impact of the blow.
There is no hard and fast rule about whether your heels should be raised or flat. It depends on several factors, such as body position, whether you are attacking or defending, your reaction, etc. Ultimately, you want to retain complete balance and keep your guard up. You should not be flat-footed in motion but should glide on the balls of your feet with sensitivity and feeling.

#BruceLee #KungFuTuesdays #GungFuTuesdays #GungFu #KungFu #martialarts #fightingmethods #jkd #jeetkunedo #footwork

🐉 Kung Fu Tuesdays ‘Some Philosophy for Martial Artists’:

May martial artists be more interested in the root of martial arts and not the different decorative branches, flowers or leaves. When you understand the root, you understand all its blossoming. Please do not be concerned with soft versus firm, kicking versus striking, grappling versus hitting and kicking, long-range versus infighting. There is no such thing as ‘this’ is better than ‘that’. Truth in the way of combat is perceived from moment to moment when there is awareness without condemnation, justification or identification. This is possible only through self-exploration in free expression and not in imitative repetition of an imposed pattern of movement. Face reality and not a crystallization of form. The tool is a tool of formless form.

#brucelee #martialarts #martialartists #theroot #kungfutuesdays #gungfutuesdays #formlessform

In 1968, Mark Rothko experienced a life-changing medical episode. His doctor told him he needed to change four things to improve his health: stop drinking, stop smoking, clean up his diet and paint nothing larger than 40 inches.

‘He did one of the four’, says art advisor Andrew Fabricant.

From 1968 until his death in 1970, Rothko made hundreds of paintings on paper, primarily under 40 inches. He personally chose a select group of these paintings to be shown and sold during his lifetime. Of these, ‘Untitled’ — with its fiery reds, pinks and slash of white — is an exceptional example. Notably, Rothko used acrylic, a newly-adopted medium in his oeuvre, which allowed him speed, freedom and layers of luminosity. The result was profound. 

In this conversation between Fabricant and Kat Widing, Senior Specialist, Post-War and Contemporary Art, discover the story behind a vital work made during Rothko’s final years.

BREAKING NEWS
The Norwegian Nobel Committee has decided to award the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career. Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion. A common thread runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.

This year’s laureate has significantly enlarged the scope and impact of international law. She has served as a judge on the High Court in South Africa, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She was the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and, until recently, she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Today Navi Pillay is a judge on the International Court of Justice in the case where Myanmar stands accused of genocide.

Navi Pillay is one of the great defenders of international legal principles in our time. Her distinguished career reminds us of the need to support, fortify and expand the global rule of law. Navi Pillay’s commitment to justice and human dignity is a source of hope and inspiration to all who seek to bring about a more peaceful world.

Learn more about the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize by clicking the link in our bio.

2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career. Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion. A common thread runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.

This year’s laureate has significantly enlarged the scope and impact of international law. She has served as a judge on the High Court in South Africa, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She was the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and, until recently, she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Today Navi Pillay is a judge on the International Court of Justice in the case where Myanmar stands accused of genocide.

In historic international court cases, she has shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence. Navi Pillay has also contributed to strengthen the institutions of international law. Her independence, expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time.

Learn more about the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize by clicking the link in bio. 

#NobelPeacePrize #NobelPrize

In awarding this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, the Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law – national and international – underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently. Peace requires justice.

History has shown that a world operating without the rule of law is unjust, unwise and inhumane. The judges – those who guard the thin red line between order and chaos – are therefore highly deserving of our praise. But today, as these same judges are sanctioned, and their institutions are attacked, we need people of courage, vision and determination – qualities that 2026 peace laureate Navi Pillay demonstrates in her work on the bench.

Navi Pillay has held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict. In all the positions she has held, she has stressed the responsibility of individuals and states to comply with the rule of law. She has also helped define the relevant norms and legal principles. When the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide – her influence was a significant factor. In the same case, Ms Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough: for the first time, a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely on the basis of spreading propaganda.

The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 springs directly from Alfred Nobel’s will. Navi Pillay strengthens fraternity between nations and – by systematically advancing the use of tribunals for peace and justice – she provides substance, direction and motivation for peace conferences in their modern form.

Throughout October, we'll be celebrating the different teams that help make cybersecurity what it is.

𝗣𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗺 𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁? The difference matters whether you’re hiring one or learning how they work.

Both simulate real-world attacks, but they’re designed to answer relatively different questions.

A penetration test is usually focused on finding and exploiting vulnerabilities within a defined environment, like a network, web application, or wireless environment.

A red team engagement takes a broader look at how an organization responds to a realistic adversary, including areas like detection, security controls, incident response, and overall resilience.

For security teams, that distinction can help determine which type of assessment actually fits your goals.

For aspiring pentesters and red teamers, it’s also an important reminder that the work isn’t exactly the same. One is often more focused on uncovering weaknesses within a defined scope; the other looks at how those weaknesses, defenses, and response processes hold up together.

A useful rule of thumb: if an organization hasn’t established regular penetration testing yet, that’s usually the place to start. If it’s already consistently testing and remediating findings, a red team engagement may be the logical next step.

Google — facing increasing competition from other apps like Instagram and TikTok when it comes to consumers searching for things — wants to be the first place people go for discovery and planning pastimes. In aid of that, today the company announced three new features for its star navigation app, Google Maps: aerial and more immersive views of 100 landmarks, more detailed cycling routes, and improved location sharing with notifications for the arrival and departure of your friends.

Google Maps has long been adding in more features beyond just giving you the ability to plan how to get from A to B, and even some of the features today are essentially interim steps in longer upgrade strategies. The company first introduced the idea of immersive views at its developer conference Google IO back in May with an aim to creating 3D models of landmarks by using a fusion of Street View, satellite, and aerial images. With that in mind, the company is now rolling out immersive views of more than 100 places situated in cities like Barcelona, London, New York, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

Crowdfunding isn’t Plan B anymore.⁠
⁠
@everette says the old stigma that @Kickstarter is only for founders who couldn’t raise VC is disappearing as major brands, creators and established companies increasingly turn to the platform.⁠
⁠
On the latest Build Mode, the Kickstarter CEO explains why crowdfunding deserves a place in more founders’ funding strategies.⁠

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump and top AI leaders announced a signed pledge called a “Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities” — a voluntary promise to implement more controls and safety measures as the rapid development of artificial intelligence continues. 

But there seems to be a catch — namely that the “United States” was misspelled as “Unites States” in a photo of the signed agreement the President shared to Truth Social

Meanwhile, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a “State of the Force” address on Wednesday to launch a new effort to study how war may be fought as tech advances rapidly. It’s being called Project Meridian.
Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich will co-lead the project. They’ll be joined by others from fields such as academia and policy, all working under the direction of Defense Department CTO Emil Michael. Their job is to “study the battlefields of the future” and the “weapons and technologies warfighters” may use on them, said Hegseth in a letter announcing the project.

#startups #politics #business #ai #trump

Kickstarter CEO @everette says founders should think carefully about what they’re giving up when they take venture capital — because ownership and creative independence have value, too.⁠
⁠
On the latest Build Mode, we’re talking crowdfunding, alternative funding and how founders can build without immediately giving up equity.⁠
⁠
Watch the full episode on YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts. ⁠

Taking a big check might have made building FarmboxRx easier but Ashley Tyrner-Dolce says it also could have changed the decisions she was able to make.⁠
⁠
On Build Mode, Ashley explains why staying bootstrapped gave her the control to make tough calls while breaking into the highly regulated healthcare industry.

When Synthesiaio asked TechCrunch reporter Dominic-Madori Davis if she wanted to make a digital twin, she didn’t hesitate.⁠
⁠
The AI video company created two versions of Dominic: an interactive digital twin you can talk to on TechCrunch’s website, and a personal avatar that can recite scripts in her voice. Aside from its own press officer, Dominic is the first journalist Synthesia has turned into a digital avatar.⁠
⁠
The experiment raised a much bigger question: What happens to human-facing jobs when you can send an AI version of yourself instead?⁠
⁠
⁠
Read the full article: https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/26/i-created-an-interactive-digital-avatar-of-myself-and-you-can-talk-to-it/

Founders: don’t rush to outsource sales.⁠
⁠
FarmboxRx founder Ashley Tyrner-Dolce learned firsthand that sometimes customers need to hear directly from the person building the company.⁠
⁠
Watch the full episode of Build Mode on YouTube

Meta’s AI agent Muse stole the spotlight this week, but would you trust Meta with your entire digital life? ⁠
⁠
The Equity crew looks at the company’s consumer AI ambitions and why some users (like Sean) might prefer to hand that information to another provider

Bootstrapping sometimes means getting creative just to keep the business moving.⁠
⁠
FarmboxRx founder Ashley Tyrner-Dolce shares how she managed cash flow, made payroll, and stretched every dollar while building her company without venture funding.⁠
⁠
The full episode of Build Mode is out now.

Is the next era of cybersecurity machine vs. machine?

Shardul Shah of Index Ventures tells Equity that as AI-powered attacks get faster and cheaper, human-in-the-loop defense won’t be enough. The result could be an entirely new security stack.

Would you take your startup public this early?

Archer has raised nearly $4 billion, and CEO Adam Goldstein says going public was an “amazing decision” he’d make again every single time.
But there’s a tradeoff: once you’re public, you have to show investors meaningful progress every 90 days.

Hear why Archer made the bet and what other founders can learn from it on the latest episode of Build Mode.

Watch the full episode at the link in bio.

AI leaders are suddenly talking about "pacing the frontier," but the specifics are still pretty fuzzy.

Equity breaks down why we're skeptical that the AI industry is actually headed for a slowdown, even as leaders at Anthropic and OpenAI say they want to put the brakes on.

Bluecore Energy announced Tuesday an oversubscribed $50 million seed round — just months after raising a $10 million pre-seed and coming out of stealth. 

As TechCrunch previously reported, the company, founded earlier this year by Kofi Asante, builds small nuclear reactors (SMRs) on floating barges, rather than fixed locations, to generate clean energy for ports and nearby infrastructure. This means that energy can be transported to wherever it is needed, an idea Asante hopes can bring clean power to those who need it most. 

“My philosophy is that access to clean energy and also clean water should be a human right,” he said.

Tan Suan: Reshaping Time Beneath Light and Shadow

Being seen can happen in an instant. Becoming yourself takes time. Beyond the camera, time has continued to shape @tan__suan’s taste, expression and sense of self.

Her journey from “being looked at” to “expressing herself” reflects a wider shift among a new generation of young women creators taking control of their own narratives.

For Hypebeast China’s latest digital cover, we step beyond the frame with Tan Suan to see how time continues to reshape her. Head to the link in bio to read our full cover story with Tan Suan.

———

【碳酸：光影之下，時間的重塑】

被看見只是一瞬間，成為自己卻需要很久。鏡頭記錄 @tan__suan 的當下，時間則在鏡頭之外，塑造她的審美、表達與自我認知。

從「被看」到「去表達」，碳酸的成長，也是當下年輕女性創作者正在經歷的轉變。那些曾經在鏡頭裡被觀看的精緻客體，開始掌握自己的敘事方式，建立自己的文化表達。

當越來越多中國年輕創作者帶著自己的審美與經驗走向世界，她們也正在從被定義的人，成為語境的參與者。

光影之下，時間正在重塑她。Hypebeast 最新封面故事，與碳酸一起，退回鏡頭之外，看見時間如何重塑一個人。

A new season in seven works. Discover highlights from MAWASIM: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art.

Meaning ‘seasons’ in Arabic, MAWASIM not only marks Christie’s first fine-art auction in Abu Dhabi, but also a new chapter in the region.

Bringing together 70 works, the auction celebrates the rich artistic exchanges across the Middle East and Africa and the diverse practices that have shaped the region’s modern and contemporary art landscape. Among the highlights are works by Faisal Liabi Sahi, Fahrelnissa Zeid, Mohammed Chabâa, Mahmoud Saïd, Ayman Baalbaki, Ali Banisadr and Saliba Douaihy.

View highlights at Christie’s London, 8–14 October, followed by the full pre-auction exhibition at The Abu Dhabi EDITION, 28 October–1 November 2026.

🗓 MAWASIM: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art | The Abu Dhabi EDITION | 1 November

موسم جديد في سبعة أعمال فنية. اكتشفوا أبرز أعمال "مواسم: 20 عاماً من الفن الحديث والمعاصر في الشرق الأوسط".

Happy Saudi National Day 🇸🇦 
 
Today, we join in celebrating the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s 96th National Day — honouring its history, cultural heritage, and enduring artistic legacy.
 
From its rich traditions to its dynamic contemporary arts scene, Saudi culture continues to evolve while staying rooted in the history and identity shaped by the Kingdom’s unification in 1932.
 
Featured here is Abdul Halim Radwi’s Khibayti (1994), a rare hand-carved wooden work depicting a traditional folk performing arts from western Saudi Arabia. Through its synthesis of figuration and abstraction, the work offers a powerful reflection of Saudi identity. 
 
The work will be offered at MAWASIM: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art in Abu Dhabi on 1 November

Twenty years. A new season.

In 2006, Christie’s held its inaugural Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art auction in Dubai, as the first plans for Saadiyat Cultural District were taking shape.

 Twenty years on, MAWASIM: 20 years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art marks a new season for Christie’s in the region. Bringing together more than 70 works spanning six decades of artistic practice, the sale reflects on the evolution of the category over the past two decades and the vibrant ecosystem of artists, collectors, galleries and institutions that continues to shape the region’s artistic future.

From pioneering modernism to contemporary experimentation, the sale features works from prestigious collections including the Dalloul Collection, Beirut, and Barjeel Art Foundation, Sharjah.

This anniversary auction will take place in Abu Dhabi on 1 November, accompanied by a programme of exhibitions, talks and events as the city’s cultural season begins.

Highlights will be on view in New York, Paris and London before the exhibition at The Abu Dhabi EDITION, from 28 October to 1 November.

🗓️ Mawasim: 20 years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art | Abu Dhabi | 1 November 

 
في عام 2006، أقامت دار كريستيز أول مزاد لها للفن الحديث والمعاصر من الشرق الأوسط في دبي، بالتزامن مع بدء تبلور المخططات الأولى للمنطقة الثقافية في السعديات.
 
وبعد عشرين عامًا، يشكّل مزاد «مواسم: 20 عامًا من الفن الحديث والمعاصر من الشرق الأوسط» بداية موسم جديد لكريستيز في المنطقة. ويجمع المزاد أكثر من 70 عملًا فنيًا تمتد عبر ستة عقود من الممارسة الفنية، مستعرضًا تطوّر هذا المجال خلال العقدين الماضيين، والمنظومة الحيوية من الفنانين وجامعي الأعمال الفنية وصالات العرض والمؤسسات التي تواصل رسم ملامح المستقبل الفني للمنطقة.
 
ومن روّاد الحداثة إلى التجارب المعاصرة، يضم المزاد أعمالًا من مجموعات مرموقة، من بينها مجموعة دلّول في بيروت، ومؤسسة بارجيل للفنون في الشارقة.
 
ويُقام هذا المزاد الاحتفالي في أبو ظبي يوم 1 نوفمبر، بالتزامن مع انطلاق الموسم الثقافي في المدينة، ويرافقه برنامج من المعارض والجلسات والفعاليات.
 
كما ستُعرض مجموعة من أبرز الأعمال في نيويورك وباريس ولندن، قبل انتقالها إلى المعرض المقام في فندق ذا أبو ظبي إديشن، خلال الفترة من 28 أكتوبر إلى 1 نوفمبر.

Christie’s is saddened to learn of the passing of Sliman Mansour, one of the defining figures of contemporary Arab art, aged 79.

Reflecting on his remarkable career and enduring impact, Dr. Ridha Moumni, Chairman, Middle East & Africa, remarked: 

“Mansour gave form to the deepest feelings of the Palestinian people through his unmistakable work. For over fifty years he gave relief to their spirit and stature to their land, leaving behind some of the most iconic paintings from the Arab world. His legacy is permanent.”

A remarkable gathering takes shape in Venice.

The National Pavilion of Qatar has announced untitled 2026 (a gathering of remarkable people) for the 61st International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia.

Commissioned by Her Excellency Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Chairperson of Qatar Museums, and led by Rirkrit Tiravanija, the presentation brings together works by Sophia Al-Maria, Tarek Atoui, Alia Farid and Fadi Kattan.

Through film, sculpture, sound, performance and food, the project will transform the future site of the permanent Qatar Pavilion into a space for artistic exchange — celebrating the creative voices of the Arab world and the enduring power of culture to bring people together.

The National Pavilion of Qatar | La Biennale di Venezia | Open until 22 November

Gulf Now
 
Marking two decades since Christie’s inaugural Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art auction, this online sale brings together pioneering modern masters and exciting contemporary voices from the region.

A specially curated section, Gulf Now, explores the breadth of contemporary artistic practice across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar. Featuring established figures including Ahamed Mater, Abdulnasser Gharem, and Mohammed Kazem alongside emerging talents Sara Abdu, Mubarak Al Thani, and Bouthayna Al Muftah, the selection offers a compelling perspective on the Gulf’s evolving cultural landscape.

Together, these artists challenge convention, spark dialogue, and redefine the visual language of the Gulf for a new generation.

🔗Learn more via the link in bio.

📅 Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art Online | 2–16 June | London

This is not just abstraction. It’s the start of a new postcolonial modernism.

Painted in early 1960s Rome, Mohamed Melehi’s ‘64 Quadrattini’ captures a pivotal moment in the artist’s practice — where colour, rhythm and geometry shape a visual language informed by both international abstraction and local cultural identity.

A luminous red field, bordered in black and punctuated by a sequence of small coloured squares, the work balances stillness with vibration — signalling ideas that would come to define Melehi’s career and the development of modern Moroccan art.
